hints.title: Unsorted Local Extremum Obstacle
hints.text: The array is not globally sorted, making conventional targets inapplicable. How does comparing midpoint with its immediate neighbor point toward guaranteed local ascent?

hints.title: Slope Ascent Invariant
hints.text: If nums[mid] < nums[mid + 1], an uphill slope exists toward the right, guaranteeing at least one peak on the right half. Otherwise, a peak lies at or to the left.

hints.title: Ascent Convergence Procedure
hints.text: Set left = 0 and right = len(nums) - 1. While left < right, evaluate mid = (left + right) // 2. If nums[mid] < nums[mid + 1], set left = mid + 1. Otherwise set right = mid. When left == right, return left.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 1000)
complexity.notes: Logarithmic convergence along local gradient slope in O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Linear scan takes O(N) operations which does not satisfy the strict O(log N) requirement.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant auxiliary pointers operate directly on the given array.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing that neighboring boundaries at -infinity ensure an ascent always terminates at a peak.
